text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Troops, tipped off about an impending attack, got ahead of "terrorists" to a hamlet south of Algiers and foiled their attempt to massacre villagers there. The soldiers killed two gunmen and wounded three as a group of about 30 moved into the village near Larba, 25 km (15 miles) from the Algerian capital at the weekend. The rest fled into mountains nearby.
- Opposition deputies in the National Assembly (lower house) hit at the government programme, with some saying it was an ideological patchwork peppered with economic targets, unlikely to be achieved.

- Partisan political motives weigh down on the assembly debate of the government programme. (Islamist-oriented) Movement of a Peaceful Society (MPS) is straddling the government and opposition camps. (MPS is represented in the cabinet by seven ministers and some of its deputies publicly criticised the government programme).
- The assembly debate of the government programme bares MPS's contradictions.
- Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia seeks to convince deputies that his cabinet is striving to tackle the country's main issues within the realms of possibility.
